utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Why have you reviewed those editions?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: As part of the investigation, it came to my attention that there were previous publications of protected material in the Slobodna Dalmacija which had a relevance to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, because there is no link between the text published in Slobodna Dalmacija newspaper and the allegations against Mr. Marijacic and Mr. Rebic. I would appreciate it if we could concentrate on the charges in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. If Ms. Graham could explain to us the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, one of the issues that was discussed this morning in the Pre-Trial Conference was the dissemination of the 2000 -- the December 2000 order and the awareness that the accused had of this order. The testimony that this witness is about to give goes to this matter directly. He's going to talk about the dissemination of this order and about the awareness that the accused, especially the accused Ivica Marijacic, had of this order. And he's conducted a detailed review of all of these editions and can quite quickly explain to Your Honours how Exhibit 36, which is the exhibit containing all of this material, works, the contents of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will allow the Prosecution to lead the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, can you just briefly explain what was published in Slobodna Dalmacija in November and December 2000.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: In November of 2000, Slobodna Dalmacija published excerpts of the witness statement of a protected witness. That was followed by an order by the Blaskic Trial Chamber to cease and desist. During December of 2000, Slobodna Dalmacija continued, despite the order, to publish 22 separate segments of the verbatim trial transcripts, the closed-session trial transcripts of the protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And, Witness, did Slobodna Dalmacija publish the 2000 order?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Before we get to that, maybe I can just have the witness provided with a copy of Exhibit 36 in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, can you explain how the Prosecution came into possession of this material?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: The original material came to us by way of Zagreb field office. The normal course of action is our people in Zagreb would review the local publications for matters of interest. Upon seeing this, then they would contact the particular trial attorney - in this case it was the Blaskic trial team - and relay that information down, usually by way of fax.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, just looking at tab 1 that you have in front of you there. Quickly looking at the B/C/S version we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's in binder 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: It's in binder 3, yes, Your Honour. Exhibit P36 in binder 3, yes. There's a series of, I think, 28 tabs under that exhibit heading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, down the bottom of the page on tab number 1 appears the date 24 May 2005. Can you explain why that date's there?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes. During the course of investigation, I also, as an investigative tool, use the Internet. I accessed Slobodna Dalmacija's Internet archives, where I located a series of publications, or reproductions of the publications for the dates in question for November and for December 2000, those publications containing, in November, the witness statement of the protected witness and, in December, a copy of the court order as well as the closed-session trial transcripts of the protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: So to clarify, Witness, this document is one that you downloaded from the Internet.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: This B/C/S document, yes, from the Internet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So where are the ones -- where are the ones that were faxed to the office? Because there will now be an issue over whether the Internet is publishing identical material to the actual physical publication.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have those before me, Your Honour, but the original ones that were sent down by Internet were used by the Blaskic Prosecution in their motions of November of 2000 which led to the Blaskic Trial Chamber's order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're now talking about the post-order, post-December 2000 order publication of the 22 segments of the verbatim trial transcripts. Now, why haven't we got the published material?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, for this edition we have the initial version of Slobodna Dalmacija, which I was going to propose showing quickly to the witness for him to explain how the material is reproduced. So if I can have the witness provided with the first 27. And, Your Honours, appearing on the computer evidence channel is also a scan of this image which might be easier to see visually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which tab is that particular edition?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: This tab it tab 1 of the binders. It's the 27th of November 2000 edition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So that's in the first volume of the binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: No. This is all in volume 3 of the binders. In volume 3 of the binders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mine starts at 33 in volume 3. 36.1 is an article of the 27th of November 2000, which isn't the one that we're about to deal with?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is what we're dealing with at the moment. I just wanted to clarify with the witness and get him to correspond as an example how the material published in Slobodna Dalmacija on the -- what we have in the binders, the B/C/S in the binders corresponds with the original version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is before the -- this is material before the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: This is before the order, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, can you just explain what's shown on the cover of this edition of Slobodna Dalmacija.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes. On the top portion, there's a photograph of the courtroom setting, and it's titled "Transkripti iz Haaga"; "Transcripts of The Hague."

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And can you identify from the cover where the article appears in the edition?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: On page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And turning to page 7 now, and if we can bring up page 7 in Sanction as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just ask that this material not be broadcast outside the courtrooms, this -- what's being shown on the Sanction screen at the moment, because this relates to a witness who has not had protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm afraid it has been already. It was on the ELMO? No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: It appears before you in the courtroom but not appearing outside of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And, Witness, if you can just turn to the B/C/S translation of -- so leaving page 7 on the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is an open session but we're not revealing the content or identity of the protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: That's exactly right, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But I'm afraid the ELMO is not working. So why don't we use the computer evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Yes, if you use the computer evidence channel. I think the ELMO is just assisting the witness to be able to turn the pages of the paper at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So let us go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: So, Witness, if you can have a look again in tab 1, in the paper copy that you've got there, and have a look at the B/C/S version there.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: This is an accurate reproduction.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I come back to the question of what kind of order this is. Let's assume, just for the sake of argument, that somebody's actually managed to pick up the identity of the witness that is the subject of protection. What order would prevent publication of that?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Of the material the witness is discussing at the moment, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: That witness is protected by the 6th of June decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's already an order --

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Exactly. There is an order in force, Your Honour, yes, which hasn't been listed at the moment, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I'd like to make sure whether Defence is able to follow in the computer evidence. You are able to see the monitor through the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we can see the computer channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about -- how about the accused? Are they able to follow? I see them nodding. Yes, please go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Okay. If I could have the 27th of November edition removed from the witness. We've finished dealing with that edition now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was confused with the date which appears on the right bottom of the B/C/S version. That's the date of a downloading.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the witness just said, so I was just corresponding for Your Honours how what the witness downloaded matches what is located the editions of Slobodna Dalmacija.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, maybe I could just add to that. Where did you locate this material on the Internet?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: This was through the website of Slobodna Dalmacija. There's a tab where you can click to go to their archives, and you can check the archives by date.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And, Witness, is this material still on the website of Slobodna Dalmacija?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: As far as I am aware, no. Once I located this material, I contacted the former editor of Slobodna Dalmacija and asked him to voluntarily remove it, which he took steps to do so, and I believe it was the 11th of June was -- it was gone.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And just to clarify, you showed us in the example a minute ago of tab 1. Can you clarify whether the other tabs in Exhibit P36, where there's Internet printing, whether they match what's in the physical editions of Slobodna Dalmacija.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Most of the other ones are not taken from the Internet. The others ones have been taken from the motions, material that the OTP Blaskic trial team would have received from Zagreb. If you look at the 28th of November, you'll see that the B/C/S was part of the initial motion in order to obtain the order. You'll see -- in the top you'll see the case -- the case number.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And, Witness, have you reviewed all of the tabs in this binder?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And have you reviewed all the physical copies available to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And can you confirm that what's in the binders is a true and accurate representation of what's in the papers?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask two questions. First of all of you: Does the article that's the subject of the case not acknowledge knowledge of the orders?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, it does acknowledge knowledge of the orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask Mr. Ivanovic a question. Does Mr. Marijacic dispute that he knew about all three orders?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The order in question was issued in closed session. None of the orders here pertains to the matters -- the matter of this case. They do not refer to the protection of the identity of Van Kuijk. They do not pertain to Hrvatski List. None of these orders specifies the name of Mr. Marijacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not my question, Mr. Ivanovic. If you would listen to the question carefully. Do you dispute -- does Mr. Marijacic dispute that he knew of the existence of the three orders? It's a separate question who they apply to. Did he know of the existence? Does he dispute that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we dispute that, Your Honour, because the orders were issued in closed session. Mr. Marijacic could not have knowledge of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: At the time of publication he disputes knowledge of these orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The order of the 6th of June was not known to him. It was issued on an ex parte basis, in a closed session. Likewise, he was not aware of the oral order from December 1997, and he was also unaware of the order from 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Except through the media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So he did know through the media, which is what the Prosecution at the moment are trying to prove.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As any other person who had access and read the papers. I don't know how we are going to prove whether he actually read or did not read the papers. However, of course once the orders were made public, appeared publicly, yes, he was aware of their existence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's what I thought, and I just have to ask myself what all this evidence is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree with you, Your Honour. This has nothing to do with the merits of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Graham.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, it sounds, as Judge Bonomy just noted, that the accused -- we weren't aware that they agreed to this particular point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think you can read that into it, Ms. Graham, but that depends how you read all that's gone before in the case. But I don't think the position's as clear cut as to divert you from the course of action you've decided to take. It's a pity that this is necessary, but I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Yes, and thank you very much, Your Honour, for clarifying that this is definitely an issue, and I'll try to make this as brief as possible. I'll go now to the, I think, potentially crucial tab of P36, which is P36, tab 5, in the binders. And if the witness can just turn to that in his copies as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Just going through this piece by piece, Witness, can you just explain what is produced on pages 1 to 7 of the English translation of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Page 1 to 7 are excerpts from the trial transcript in the Blaskic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And then what appears after that?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It goes into private session, and this is where the trial team requests closed session for the protective witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And that's a different protected witness from Van Kuijk?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Yes. And so after sections of the transcript is set out, what is contained in the article after that?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: On pages 8 to 11 in the English is a copy of the December 1, 2000 cease and desist order issued by the Blaskic Chambers.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Maybe at this point we could just bring those up on the Sanction computer in B/C/S firstly, that is pages 8 to 10 on Sanction, of the B/C/S version of Exhibit P36, tab 5. So if you -- Witness, are you looking at the computer evidence on your screen at the moment?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I only see the transcript of this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Looking at the bottom of the page -- right. Okay. Oh, excellent. I see. And what can you see now?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I can see the issue of -- the B/C/S issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And what appears on the bottom of the screen?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: At the bottom of the screen is the B/C/S version of the court order I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And maybe if we can just quickly show pages 9 and 10 of the B/C/S version in Sanction too. Does the order continue on these pages?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: These bold headings, are they part of the order?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: No, they're not. I believe these would have been inserted by the publication itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Apart from those headings, though, is all of the 3rd -- is all of the 1st of December, 2000 order reproduced in this edition of Slobodna Dalmacija?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: If I can now have -- Witness, if you could now turn to tab 6 in your documents, which is P36, tab 6. And if we can just show the B/C/S quickly in Sanction. And if, Witness, you can have a look at the English version. And maybe we can show actually in Sanction now the second page of the English translation. Witness -- actually, we'll show the first page of the English translation as well first. Witness, can you explain what appears in this edition of Slobodna Dalmacija?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: This is an article headed by Bisera Lusic, and it is entitled "The Hague Sues Slobodna Dalmacija," and the subject is "Position of Slobodna Dalmacija Editor-in-chief Josip Jovic regarding the Tribunal's order to stop publication of" the protected witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And then what's appearing if we go to the second page of the English? What have we got on this page?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It appears to be a quote from Josip Jovic: "I have no moral obligations to The Hague."

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And if I can just have the witness shown the hard copy edition of this version of Slobodna Dalmacija. Your Honours, I have actually made photocopies for the Court of this relevant pages of this edition of Slobodna Dalmacija. I would have made copies for the 3rd of December edition but we don't have that within the Prosecution. I think it will assist if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is exactly the concern that I expressed during the Pre-Trial Conference when I agreed with your position and the position of His Honour Judge Bonomy. Just look at where this is going, where we are being led. What is sought to be proved? We're going to discuss testimonies of other protected witnesses. We're going to debate statements of other journalists, other editors. Why? For the Prosecution to prove that Mr. Marijacic was aware of the order of 2000? Or is it their assumption that he read the papers and that he must have read this in the papers? We are going to waste a lot of time, and this is exactly what I was afraid would happen to us when I told you that I was even prepared to drop my witnesses, because I thought the matter was quite simple, and it really involved one single legal issue. However, this is not what we are going to do today, and with all due respect, I see that the Court is allowing the OTP to conduct -- to lead evidence which, in my humble opinion, is not what the matter is all about. The matter is rather simple, and that is whether the contents of the testimony were protected and whether it was the content of the testimony that was published by the accused or not. Having said that, Your Honours, I'm fully prepared to abide by any decision that Your Honours intend to make on the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I understand the Defence position. The Defence position would be that the third order, of 1st of December in 2000, is not applicable to these accused, but it is the Prosecution's case it is still applicable to this case and it is open for them to prove that accused were aware of this order unless the Defence concede that they were aware of this -- the existence of this order. So please go on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The problem here is not one from, I think, principally for Mr. Rebic. It's one for Mr. Marijacic, because it's claimed in the pre-trial brief by the Prosecution that Mr. Marijacic was actually working for this newspaper at the time these publication -- these articles were being written. And, you know, common sense again would suggest that it's a fair inference that he would be reading his own newspaper. But if that can't be agreed, then obviously the Prosecution have got to prove it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour, on the assumption that everybody's acting on their common sense. I am inclined to think that the majority of people are not always acting on their common sense, and moreover, they're not aware of the legal applications involved in this matter. I don't know if it is necessary for us to engage in the psychological or psychiatric discussion whether those who read these articles necessarily understand the intention, and so on and so forth. We also need to -- in that case we need to decide whether the position is the same now as it was in 2001. And then we also would have to take into account the case law of this Tribunal then and now, and so on and so forth. It is my opinion, Your Honours, with all due respect, that this is not relevant. However, if it is your decision to allow this evidence to proceed, then I fully respect it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless the Defence is ready to agree with the fact that Defence were -- the accused were aware of the existence of this order, the Prosecution has to prove it. But please go on. You can deal with it very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This really won't take much longer. But I would like to have the witness shown the hard copy edition for the 4th of December, and I also have copies for the Trial Chamber of what -- the relevant sections of this edition, as well as a translation of those relevant sections. And can I confirm, Your Honours, that Sanction is not being broadcast for this portion of the evidence, for everything dealing with P36, Exhibit P36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Technical booth should have noted that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And, Usher, I have copies for Their Honours and the other parties in the courtroom as well. And if the witness can also be given a copy of the translation as well. And if I can have Sanction display the cover of this edition for the 4th of December, but not broadcast outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, can you just explain what appears on the cover of this 4th of December edition of Slobodna Dalmacija without identifying any protected witness.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: On the top right-hand corner there's a banner that says "Slobodnoj Dalmaciji Sitze Haaska Tuzba," which is "Slobodna Dalmacija --" "The Hague Sues Slobodna Dalmacija," and it shows that the article is to appear on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: So turning to page 2 of the exhibit. Is what is shown on page 2, does that match what we were looking at a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies, but I have to do what I'm supposed to do here. If you have the English version of this text and of this cover page, you will understand my question. What is the link between these two texts? Here we have a weekly that is called Globus, and then we have the daily Slobodna Dalmacija. Two editors. One is saying, "I have no moral obligation towards The Hague," and the other is saying something similar. What is the link between this and Mr. Marijacic and in particular Mr. Rebic? Where is the connection between the two and where is this going? My position is that Mr. Rebic did not read Slobodna Dalmacija, this particular issue for sure, because he does not read Slobodna Dalmacija. But there is another very dangerous thing. We are not allowed to publish the name of a protected witness published here in this paper, however, the order was in the paper, and it is argued, it is alleged that they were able to see and read the order in the paper. Whether this was published or not, when was this downloaded from Internet? I am completely at a loss here. I don't know where this is going. We're not allowed to mention anything contained in this article, yet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That goes to the weight of this witness's evidence. It is for the Defence to argue, to challenge later, during the cross-examination or in one way or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. I understand. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Judge Robinson has a point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Graham, can you just say what you're seeking to establish by this.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. I'm seeking both to show the extent of coverage that was given to this order and discussions of this order, which is I think relevant to both accused in this case, especially as will be established in argument later in relation to Mr. Rebic and the role that he was performing at that time, but also as His Honour Judge Bonomy noted before, we have alleged in the indictment that Marijacic was a journalist working for Slobodna Dalmacija, and I'm about to get to the extent of his involvement in the paper after showing very briefly two further editions such as Your Honour has just seen which show the prominence given to this issue in Slobodna Dalmacija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Very well, yes. Move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Can I have the witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, can you turn to tab 6 in your documents there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And while the witness is looking at -- actually, we've just looked at tab 6. I mean tab 7 in your documents. And if while the witness is looking at that I can have distributed a copy of the 6th of December edition of Slobodna Dalmacija as well as copies of the front -- of the relevant pages for Their Honours and the parties and a translation of the bits in addition to the articles.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, just while this material is being distributed, can I ask you to turn to page -- can I ask you to just quickly identify what appears on pages 1 to the top of page 6 of the English translation in tab 6 -- tab 7.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: This is excerpts from the court testimony of the protected witness -- [B/C/S on English channel].

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: We just appeared to have interference from the B/C/S line. Maybe if you could start again, Witness.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: These are excerpts of the transcripts from the Blaskic trial in relation to a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And turning to page 6 of the translation, and 7, what appears on these two pages?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: This is an insert entitled "Six Reasons Why Slobodna is Publishing Testimony of the Protected Witness."

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And who is the author of that excerpt?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Josip Jovic, the editor-in-chief of Slobodna Dalmacija.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And the next article after that, is it related to what appears before?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. If we can now have shown on Sanction the cover of the edition for the 6th of December. And, Witness, looking at your translation, and just to make sure once again that this isn't being broadcast, can you just explain what is advertised on this cover.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: You see a large photo with three people in it and the headline is "Slobodna Reveals The Hague Secret."

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And turning to the next page in Sanction. Does this correspond with what we were just looking at in tab 7?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Just moving on now to the final -- well, actually before -- before we move on to another tab, Witness, I have now, if we can distribute to the Court, I have a chart that you have prepared.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is just a demonstrative exhibit to assist the witness to quickly explain some other key points in relation to this material.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, can I first ask you, how did you prepare this document?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: As part of the process of identifying in what publications and in what format, whether it be the original publication or whether it be in electronic archives, what material, whether it be the witness statement or the closed-session trial transcripts of the protected witness have been covered in those issued. In addition to that, it was also to determine how often articles appeared that were authored by or attributed to Mr. Marijacic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And looking at the fourth column along, entitled "Article by Marijacic," these are all the articles that you identified?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Just looking between -- for starters, I note that this starts on the 31st of October, 2000. Can you just explain why there's some editions there before the 27th of November?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It was to establish that Mr. Marijacic had association to Slobodna Dalmacija both prior to and after the publications of the protected material. In other words, so that we could definitively say it wasn't just several articles during that time period but before and after as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And, Witness, I note that there's some date gaps in there, like between the 16th of November, 2000, and the 27th of November, 2000. Can you explain why there's such a big gap there?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: The issues prior to the 27th were taken at random.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And also, as you can see from the exhibit number, there is on occasion some tabs missing. Like, for instance, tab 5 there's nothing between the 30th of November and the 4th of December 2000. Can you explain why there's a gap there?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Because I did not have access to the material.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, just looking at the period between the 27th of November and the 29th of December, which is the period you've identified when Slobodna Dalmacija was publishing protected material, how many times during that period did you identify articles written by Marijacic?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Nine.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, if I can have you now turn, on the chart here -- on the chart for the 7th of December, 2000, which corresponds with Exhibit P36, tab 8, of the binders, I note that the article by Marijacic appears on page 2 and the trial transcript's reproduced on pages -- on page 3. If we can turn to what is tab 8 in the binders for the 7th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And if while we're turning to that once again I can ask for the assistance of the usher to provide the hard copy version and also copies of the cover and translation to the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Graham, I'm not sure whether we gathered in what capacity were these articles by Marijacic written.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: I'll clarify that with the witness if Your Honour would like. Would that be of assistance? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, did you identify whether Marijacic held a position at the paper Slobodna Dalmacija during this period?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: He was associated to Slobodna Dalmacija. I don't have his exact position, but he was associated to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: So, Witness, he was writing for the paper? Would that accurately describe what you observed?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Maybe, Witness, also to assist Their Honours, you could turn -- you could just have a quick flip through the edition to see if there is a reference to position holders at Slobodna Dalmacija. It might be the case that they don't have a headnote like the Hrvatski List edition does. It's okay, Witness. We'll leave that.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I don't find any.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can just have a look at what once again appears in tab 8 of the hard copies you were given separately and just identify what appears on pages 1 to 8 of that translation in English.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: This is the transcript from The Hague, confidential testimony of protected witness before the court in The Hague, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And what -- what commences on page 8 of the translation?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: There is an article by Mr. Marijacic entitled "Defenders, officers, and Croats from BiH, possible assassins of protected witness."

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Just to clarify, Witness, the person who Marijacic is writing about, is it the same person whose transcript is printed above?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can now just show on the computer evidence channel, but not broadcast, the front cover of the 7th of December edition for Slobodna Dalmacija. Witness, once again can you just explain what appears on the cover here.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: The main headline, under the words "Slobodna Dalmacija," is "Transcripts from The Hague, secret testimony of the protected witness before the courts in The Hague in March 1998."

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And moving to the next page of the edition and the page after, is this the article by Marijacic we were just looking at?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And on the page after that? What do we have published there?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: This is excerpts from the closed-session transcripts of the protected witness in the Blaskic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, that was all I was going to cover with Exhibit P36 in the binders. I would ask if the tabs of that binder could be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: These six tabs.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the six tabs are the crucial tabs, up to tab 8, but I would ask that, on the basis that the witness has reviewed all the material and has confirmed that the remainder of the articles set out additional publications of protected material, that without going through each tab they could be admitted and given whatever weight Your Honours would seek to give them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Has the review of the others been done simply of the Internet pages or was there some comparison in these cases also with the actual newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Maybe I can ask the witness, based on his chart, to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, we've looked at editions up to the 7th of December 2000. Just looking at the rest of the chart there to the 29th, have you all of the -- all of the tab numbers identified here, have you reviewed all of those editions in either hard copy or in the archive?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, I have, and they're all consistent.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Okay. And you've also reviewed the material in the binders for tab 36 and compared it with that material?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, I have, and it's consistent.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, on that basis I would ask that it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will admit them all.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder if it is an appropriate time to take a break for technical reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The exhibit we just admitted shall be given a number, one number with the same number of tabs. That will be OTP 12. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've just got three more documents to ask this witness about.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Firstly, Witness, can I ask you to take Exhibit P38, which is in your pile of documents there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And for the Court, that's -- I think that's in the start of binder 4 potentially. Yes, that's correct. It's at the start of binder 4. And I can put the cover of this edition on Sanction, but this is another article that can't be broadcast outside of this courtroom for reasons of witness protections in place in relation to a person discussed in this article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, you're now looking at Exhibit P38. Can you identify this for the Court?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes. This is an edition of Slobodna Dalmacija for the 28th of February, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And how did the Prosecution obtain this document?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: This came in through the Zagreb field office to the Office of the Prosecution, the Blaskic and Kordic trial teams.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And, Witness, who is this article by?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: The article is attributed to Ivica Marijacic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And what does it relate to?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It relates to the testimony of a protected witness. This is a different protected witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Does the article identify that protected witness?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, it does. The headline is "Mitko Naumovski, Kordic's Defence lawyer, on the controversial testimony of a protected witness."

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And is that -- is the witness identified in other places in the article as well?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the article, both on -- if you look at the English version, it's named several times on page 1 and again on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And, Witness, just turning to your chart for a moment, just to make the correlation here, the demonstrative exhibit that you created, is this referred to on your chart?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This was from the electronic archives.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: So to clarify, you've looked at this both in the electronic archives and in this form faxed from the Zagreb field office?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And do the versions in the -- the version from the Zagreb field office, is it a fair and accurate representation of what you saw on the website as well?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that be admitted into evidence, Exhibit P38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This -- this is obviously designed to establish a different point from the point that we've been dealing with so far, I take it. This is to do with a previous different trial. Now, is this not like trying to say that because somebody assaulted a person on one occasion he's likely to have assaulted them on another occasion? Is this relevant to whether the orders that we're concerned with were breached?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, my primary purpose in referring to this article was just that it's included on the document that the witness created, it's part of his review of editions and showing how the accused Marijacic was publishing articles both during the period when Slobodna Dalmacija was publishing excerpts from protected material and before and after, that he had a continuing role with Slobodna Dalmacija. As to the point that Your Honour has made about this witness being a protected witness in another case and it potentially having an impact on the way that the Court would view this case, I would -- I would submit that that is a point for argument and that the document, its main purpose in being admitted is just to show that this witness was publishing at that time and that he did publish an article that related to another protected witness at this time. As to whether -- we're not at this moment making submissions. That will be for closing, any discussion about those other matters. So if Your Honour would accept it into evidence on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And that can be given the same -- consecutive number, but the previous one, the OTP 12, and this should be OTP 13, both of them should be under seal due to the protected --

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Yes, definitely, Your Honours. Thank you for reminding me about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Turning briefly now to Exhibit P39, which is the next exhibit in Your Honours' binders. And, Witness, if you can identify that in your pile there. Have you got that before you?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Witness, can you identify this article?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, this was a Slobodna Dalmacija publication on the 2nd of March, 2001. You'll notice that the B/C/S is a copy taken from the Internet archives on the 22nd of May, 2005.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Did you take it from the archives?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I did myself, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And is this -- is this a fair and accurate representation of what you printed off the website, what's in the binder?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And can you identify who the article is authored by?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: On page 3 of the English, the article is attributed to Ivica Marijacic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And once again, if we can have this version in Sanction just showing, but this can't be broadcast for either because -- for the same reasons that P38 can't be broadcast, this one can't be broadcast either. And, Witness, can you just briefly explain what this article is about.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: The article is headed "Kordic did not attend any meetings re the attack on Ahmici." The text in the article refers to the second protected witness that we've referred to in this testimony. His name is predominant numerous times on page 3 of the English version and again on page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that this exhibit also be admitted into evidence for the same reasons as P38 was admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: So maybe that can be numbered OTP 14. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Under seal. Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Under seal, absolutely, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: The last document that I would like the witness to look at is Exhibit P44. It should still be in that 4th edition, the fourth binder that Your Honours have open at the moment. Have you identified that document, Witness?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes. Again as part of the investigations, I checked the Internet quite often and I came across this article, which I printed off in the B/C/S version in relation to Mr. Rebic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And can you identify where you found this article?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It was on a website www.index.hr/clanak.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And do you know that website, Witness?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I don't know who holds the website, however, it is a Croatian-based website to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Have you found other material on that website before?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: What types of material is located on that website?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It's mostly news articles from various publications.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And can you identify who this article was written by?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It was attributed to HINA. It doesn't -- it doesn't give a name of an author.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And do you know what HINA is?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: HINA is a news agency.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Have you come across articles by HINA before?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Many times.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And, Witness, what is this article about?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It appears to be an interview with Mr. Rebic, done by whoever authored this article, in relation to the contempt charges issued by the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: And if we could maybe just show the English version on Sanction now, and if we could highlight the highlighted text there. If you can just explain what's discussed here on the screen at the moment. Have you got the computer evidence channel? If you just press on the computer evidence channel. Can you see on the screen some highlighted material?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This appears to be a quote from Mr. Rebic: "As for revealing the secret identity of the Netherlands SFOR officer, it was Rebic's opinion that 'there was never any danger for him, neither then nor now, which is confirmed by the fact that nothing has happened to him.' "He stressed that during the publication of the questionable article in Hrvatski List newspaper, he wrote that he was 'aware of what he was doing, but certain that he was doing a service to both Croatia and himself, because he was showing that it was not true that the State of Croatia and him were involved in harbouring Bralo.'"

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that that article, this article in P44 be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to intervene most strenuously. I think it is absolutely inadmissible to suggest that this should be introduced into evidence because this is -- I hope the interpreters will manage this -- a very creative piece of work. Anybody can access the Internet, write some sort of address and publish whatever they like in whatever way they like. We all know that. There is no visible authorship, and anybody can put H-I-N-A, HINA, in brackets. This proves absolutely nothing, and this absolutely useless piece of documentation could not possibly be admissible. Until now they have at least been trying hard comparing the Internet publication with the original. Now they're going a step further. There is no proof of authenticity. I would say this is pure forgery. Do they have evidence that it isn't? What are they going to compare this with? Of course I can deal with this in cross-examination, and we will, but I think it is absolutely inadmissible to suggest even that this could be put into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you saying, Mr. Krsnik, that Mr. Rebic had never given an interview to this HINA agency to this effect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether he has given any interviews to HINA, and I cannot talk about that, but I'm absolutely certain that HINA does not publish its articles on this website but on its own website. HINA is the state news agency. They have their own website, their own Internet pages, and if they had written this article, they would have published it on their own website. We don't know whose website this is. Why would HINA publish its articles on a different address when it has its own?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It is a question of authenticity that you're primarily concerned with. You would concede that, if it is authentic, it does have material that would be relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We would like to hear from -- yes. You have further --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I maintain that authenticity is questionable because I live in a very small state and I know it very well. HINA is the official news agency of that state, and it publishes its articles on its own website. That's why I said from the beginning that I question everything, not only authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krsnik. Ms. Graham, you agree that this site is not official site of HINA news agency?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wouldn't agree that. I'm not sure whether the witness might be able to help us on the relationship between the Index website and the HINA website. We certainly -- we could adduce evidence, if Your Honours wanted, through an additional witness to explain that, and I can explain it to you, if you would like, but -- but basically Index is a website that indexes a lot of news services in Croatia, as we understand the position, and so HINA -- HINA is a big Croatian news agency. Things are broadcast, and there are other servers where things are accessible from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that's all you can respond to the submission of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Well, that's not all. As to the reliability of this document, I've explained how this witness came to find it on the website, that he knows about HINA as a Croatian news agency, and that what we have in the binders is exactly what he's printed off, and that he's found other material previously of this sort, and so it's not, you know, some unusual and far-fetched and likely-to-be-forged type of document. So, Your Honours, I would say that on those grounds that the points being raised really by Mr. Krsnik about interpretation by newspapers, these types of matters are questions of weight and they're not questions of the admissibility of this document, and that the document should be admitted and he can make those submissions in argument if he so wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I take it from the fact that it's not been addressed that no attempt was made to check with HINA whether this was authentic?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: If Your Honours would just give me a moment just to confer with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can't add anything to that at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, just -- If you would allow me just to make one more point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Graham, you would share something else?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Yes. If Your Honours would like, we can try and track down an original HINA version overnight, if that would be preferential, and we can provide that version as well as the version from Index.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having heard that, can we not defer the determination of admissibility until tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, yes. That concludes everything I wanted to ask this witness about, so ends his testimony. Just one more thing, though, Your Honours. I do have a second demonstrative exhibit like the one I provided to you at the beginning of this witness's testimony for the 18th of November, 2004, Hrvatski List edition. I've also got one for the 5th of May, 2005 Hrvatski List edition, which Your Honours have also admitted as Exhibit P48, once again just correlating the translation in English against the B/C/S, and if Your Honours would be assisted by that, I can have that distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And now for the Defence to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, I've just got one more question for you, I apologise. But just -- the demonstrative exhibit that the witness created, the chart, I'm wondering if that could be moved into evidence as it pertains to his testimony and helps to explain the evidence he's given on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, can it not work as a kind of aide-memoire?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Certainly, if Your Honour would prefer, it could be an aide-memoire, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. The Chamber will admit it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It can be given a number of OTP 15. Who shall begin? Mr. Ivanovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will introduce myself to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Marin Ivanovic. I am representing Mr. Marijacic in these proceedings. I will be much briefer than my learned colleague was. First of all, I would like to ask you, have you read all the writings of Mr. Marijacic for that period?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: No, I haven't read all of them. The articles that were found in my sampling, those were compared to what was in the papers that we did have. The ones that were relevant for the case that were translated into English I did read, but by no means did I read each and every article that he's presented in Slobodna Dalmacija.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In those articles that you have read, did Mr. Marijacic make a single mention of Mr. Van Kuijk and his testimony?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of, no, and that's one thing I looked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he ever mention the testimony of another protected witness?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Not in that context, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Has he ever written about any testimony given by protected witness Van Kuijk?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Has he ever written, in those articles that you have read, about the testimony of the person we are here referring to as the second protected witness?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of, no. None that I've seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Have you read the order of this Tribunal concerning the protection of identities of the 1st of December, 2000?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does it refer to any person, any protected witness by name?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: May I see the order, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That can be handed over to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Yes, that's Exhibit P36 in the binder. If that could be handed to the witness. It's P35 in the binders, just immediately before P36.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this order refer to any protected witness by name?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this order invoke any earlier decision of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It takes into consideration the Chamber's decision of June 6, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this order mention any media in the Republic of Croatia by name, and which?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: In mentions Globus and Slobodna Dalmacija.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does it refer to any journalists and reporters to whom this order is addressed by name?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes. From Globus it refers to Mr. Anton Masla [phoen], and Bisera Lusic on behalf of Slobodna Dalmacija.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does it refer again to Mr. Ivica Marijacic?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time when this order was issued, that is the 1st of December, 2000, was the testimony of Mr. Van Kuijk or any other witness mentioned -- sorry, published?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Not in this regard, no. Just one -- if I understand correctly, it's regarding one protected witness, not Mr. Van Kuijk.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read to me from -- or, rather, I will read from this order one excerpt, and I hope it will be interpreted. "... orders that the publication of statements or testimonies of the witness concerned and generally of any protected witness shall cease immediately." Does -- can you read this in the order?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can something cease immediately if it is happening four years later?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think it is for the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this or any similar order refer to Hrvatski List or Mr. Ivica Marijacic? Was it received by them?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It had no bearing on either Mr. Marijacic or Mr. Rebic, this particular order, by name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That question was not properly answered, but I wondered if that question can be properly answered by the witness. Let us --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: This witness isn't being called as a legal expert or anything of that nature and can't really provide testimony about the interpretation of Trial Chamber orders. So I wonder about the utility of asking him these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These questions are very helpful and our learned friends from the Prosecution, when they explained why they were introducing this material, said that they had to establish the connection with Mr. Marijacic and Mr. Rebic. I have to prove that there is no link whatsoever with Mr. Rebic or Marijacic or the incriminated event that would allow this to be included into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You can put that in legal argument, but I don't think this witness can help you on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can reformulate my question. I can rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: As an investigator for the OTP, have you ever in the course of your work come across an order that refers directly and precisely to Mr. Ivica Marijacic and Hrvatski List?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Not by name, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever as an investigator for the OTP come across an order that refers by name to the Globus publication?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: The 2001 order that I'm holding mentioned Globus.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: As an investigator for the OTP, have you ever come across an order that would refer by name to Hrvatsko Slovo?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Not until 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivanovic. Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know whether it makes sense for me to begin, because it's already half past one and I saw in the schedule that we are supposed to finish at a quarter to two. Maybe you would allow me to begin my cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long do you expect your cross-examination to run?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly more than 15 minutes. That much is true. So to avoid stopping today and continuing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us try.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. My name is Kresimir Krsnik. I'm appearing for the accused Mr. Markica Rebic here today. Mr. Cameron, you do recall your statement made on the 31st October 2005? If you don't remember it, I can place it in front of you. I know my colleagues have a copy and will be good enough to provide it in English. It's the 31st of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have it in the binder?

utterances.speaker: MS. GRAHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think, have a copy. I can check and see if we have copies available. Just one moment. Your Honours, we have one, maybe two copies with us at the moment, if that would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us get on with it. Please move on. Or we can put it on the ELMO, the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then please put the first page on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this statement contains the mention of a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now I understand, but it would not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you let me conduct my own cross-examination, I will take care, because I know what's in the statement. I kindly asked you to put page 1 on the ELMO. There is no reference to any protected witness there. Have you placed it on the ELMO? I can't see it. I would like to clear up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It should be the second button, video evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I would like to clear up right at the outset one thing that is not quite clear to me, if you could assist. I know from experience that witness statements are taken according to a certain procedure by the OTP. We have witness information listed here. Your name seems to be Terrence, last name Cameron; is that correct? And now look at the fourth line from the bottom. Names of all persons present during interviews. It says interviewer - interviewer - and then it says "Terry Cameron." Would I be wrong in understanding this as you having conducted your own interview, or is Terry Cameron a different person?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: No. It's common practice within the OTP that when an investigator provides a statement, he writes a statement out in the same format he would for any other witness, but it's done without an interpreter or another investigator as there's no need. So to respond to your question, this is my statement. I'm the person being interviewed, but I'm the person that's giving the statement and signing for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you actually wrote your own statement in your own hand without actually talking or being interviewed by anybody?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Isn't it the practice of the Office of the Prosecutor when conducting an investigation to call witnesses for an interview and then warn them of the consequences of making false statements? Isn't it the practice to caution witnesses? You haven't obviously been able to do that since you were the one who wrote the statement.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: The vast majority of the witnesses that OTP investigators deal with are either from the former Yugoslavia or elsewhere, and we have a certain preamble we use for those individuals. However, as stated earlier, when an investigator is providing his or her own statement, that's not deemed necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, this is what is -- it is this practice that the counsel is questioning. I don't quite understand it myself. Why should it be any different? But proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In my eyes, a witness is a witness. I have no reason to presume that he is different from another one. Let me just check. On page 3, there are names of certain protected witnesses, so we won't put it on the ELMO. Rather, take it in your hand. It's page 3 of your statement, paragraph 3V. Can you follow me? It's the third line from the top. "The order stipulates -" and what is meant is the order of the 6th of June, 1997 - "The order stipulates that the accused, his Defence counsel, and their representatives shall not disclose to the public or the media the names of witnesses or any other identifying information." Is that part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My question now would be: Did the Defence team honour the order of the Trial Chamber and provide a list of all persons that constituted the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: That's beyond my knowledge. That was the Blaskic trial team a number of years ago. Who or what was provided in terms of Defence or Defence team I'm not aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, you are the investigator. You were the investigator, and you were given the task of investigating the content -- sorry, the contempt case. And my learned friend Mr. Akerson must have told you that what is needed is to establish the link with Mr. Rebic and the Blaskic Defence team. I suppose that you have all the documents relevant to that. But you don't seem to have come across the one that I'm asking you about. Did the Blaskic team honour the order of the Trial Chamber and provide a list of all persons making up the Defence team? The order says: "And their personnel --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did the witness not answer the question? He said he didn't know. So let's get on with the evidence. Please move on, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree with you, of course, but he's testifying here precisely as a person who was assigned to conduct the investigation. I'm just checking. He's free to say, "I don't know," and I will accept it. I can only make my own conclusions. I don't know exactly how he proceeded with his investigation in that case, and I am precisely trying to say that he was trying all this time to establish the link with Mr. Rebic and the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Reserve your comments for your closing arguments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. Of course you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, this is not a real cross-examination, as you can see, because I'm asking you questions as if we were in examination-in-chief. Do you know what Markica Rebic was doing, and did you establish in the course of your investigation what he was doing on the 4th of December, 2000, 6th December 2000, and 7th December 2000? What was he doing on those days, where he was, and if he occupied any position, what position that was?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: You're talking about 2001?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We are precisely talking about the dates of publication of Slobodna Dalmacija. The 4th December 2000, 6th December 2000, and 7th December 2000.

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: To answer your question, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know, generally speaking, what positions Mr. Rebic occupied and how?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: The only positions that I'm aware of is I believe an assistant minister in the Croatian government, and after that, in regards to Hrvatski List, I believe he's an editor, on the editorial staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: During the investigation did you establish what "assistant minister" means? Did you mean assistant minister of defence?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, it was assistant minister of defence. I'm not totally sure. In charge of SIS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But which sector?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Honourable Court what SIS means?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: It means for security and intelligence, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know, can you tell us that first, do you know what SIS means?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I can't give you the literal translation of it, but my experience at the Tribunal is that it's an intelligence agency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I'm asking you. Did you -- in fact, you did provide a wrong translation. That's why I'm asking you if you know. If I tell you that this is a counter-intelligence service rather than an intelligence service, what would your answer be?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know the powers of that security agency within the security system, its competencies?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I wouldn't -- I have no personal experience on that. I don't know what the total competencies would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry. Do you know of the acronym H-I-S, HIS?

utterances.speaker: TERRENCE CAMERON
utterances.text: I've heard it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think our time is up, Your Honour. I would have another 15, perhaps 20 minutes of questioning. You see how fast I'm proceeding. I will continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing will be adjourned until 9.00 in the morning tomorrow.
